templates.pattern: A clock loses [L] minutes every [N] hours. It was set correctly at 8:00 AM on Monday. What is the correct time when the clock shows 8:00 AM on Wednesday?
templates.explanation: From Mon 8AM to Wed 8AM = 48 hours. Clock loses ([L]/[N]) min/hr × 48 = [L*48/N] minutes. Correct time = 8:00 AM + [L*48/N] minutes.

templates.pattern: Two clocks show the same time at 12:00 noon. Clock X gains [GX] seconds per minute. Clock Y loses [LY] seconds per minute. After how many hours will they show times exactly [DIFF] minutes apart?
templates.explanation: Per minute, X gains [GX]s and Y loses [LY]s → total divergence = ([GX]+[LY]) sec/min = ([GX]+[LY])/60 min/min. Time to diverge [DIFF] min = [DIFF] / (([GX]+[LY])/60) minutes = [DIFF]*60/([GX]+[LY]) minutes = [DIFF*60/(GX+LY)] min = [DIFF*60/(GX+LY)/60] hours.

templates.pattern: At what times between [H]:00 and [H1]:00 are the hour and minute hands of a clock perpendicular to each other?
templates.explanation: Right angle positions: M = (60H ± 15) × 2/11. For H=[H]: M1 = (60[H]+15)×2/11 and M2 = (60[H]-15)×2/11. Check if both fall between [H]:00 and [H1]:00.
answer_label: 2:27 3/11 and 2:54 6/11 (only 2:27 3/11 is valid in some interpretations)

templates.pattern: A watch which gains [G] seconds per minute was set right at 6:00 AM. What time will the watch show when the correct time is 12:00 noon?
templates.explanation: 6 hours = 360 minutes. Watch gains [G] sec/min × 360 min = [G*360] sec = [G*6] minutes. Watch shows 12:00 + [G*6] min = 12:[G*6] PM.

templates.pattern: What day of the week was [D] [MONTH] [Y]? (Use: 1 Jan 1900 = Monday)
templates.explanation: Count odd days from 1 Jan 1900 to the given date. Add to Monday. Account for leap years in the range.

templates.pattern: A clock is set to show correct time at 10:00 AM. It gains [G] min per hour. After how many hours will it show correct time again (12-hour clock)?
templates.explanation: Clock needs to gain exactly 12 hours (720 minutes) to show correct time again on 12-hr clock. Time = 720/[G] hours.

templates.pattern: If [D1] [M1] [Y1] is [DAY1], and [D2] [M2] [Y2] must be determined, what day is it? ([Y2]-[Y1] = [DIFF_Y] years, not crossing century)
templates.explanation: Count odd days in [DIFF_Y] years (including leap years in range). Add to [DAY1]. Each ordinary year = 1 odd day, each leap year = 2 odd days.

templates.pattern: A clock showed the correct time on 1st March. It lost [L] minutes on the first day, [2L] minutes on the second day, [3L] on the third... (increasing by [L] each day). How many minutes slow will it be at the end of [N] days?
How many times do the hands of a clock coincide between [T1] AM and [T2] PM on the same day?
templates.explanation: Hands coincide 11 times every 12 hours. From [T1] AM to [T2] PM: count 12-hour blocks and partial. Each 12-hr period = 11 coincidences. 24-hr period = 22.

templates.pattern: If the date [D1] [MONTH1] falls on [DAY1], what date in [MONTH2] of the same year falls on [DAY2]? (Same year, no leap year complication)
templates.explanation: Count days from [D1] [MONTH1] to [MONTH2], find the day of 1st of [MONTH2], then count to next [DAY2].

templates.pattern: A wall clock and a table clock both show correct time at 12:00 noon. The wall clock gains [GW] sec per minute and the table clock loses [LT] sec per minute. After how many minutes will the wall clock be exactly [D] minutes ahead of the table clock?
templates.explanation: Wall gains [GW]/60 min per min. Table loses [LT]/60 min per min. Combined divergence = ([GW]+[LT])/60 min per real minute. Time for [D] min gap = [D] × 60/([GW]+[LT]) real minutes.

templates.pattern: In which years between [Y1] and [Y2] does [D] [MONTH] fall on a Sunday?
templates.explanation: Find the day for each year in range. Day advances by 1 for ordinary years and 2 for leap years. Identify years where the result is Sunday.

templates.pattern: The minute hand of a clock is [M_LEN] cm long and the hour hand is [H_LEN] cm long. How far does the tip of the minute hand travel in [N] hours?
templates.explanation: Minute hand makes 1 full revolution per hour. Distance per hour = 2π × [M_LEN]. In [N] hours = 2π × [M_LEN] × [N] cm.

templates.pattern: A person was born on February 29, [Y_BIRTH] (leap year). How many actual birthdays (Feb 29) will he celebrate by [Y_NOW]?
templates.explanation: Count leap years from [Y_BIRTH] to [Y_NOW] inclusive (excluding birth year itself since that's not a birthday yet). Each leap year = 1 birthday. Note 1900 not a leap year; 2000 is.

templates.pattern: Clock A strikes every [A] hours, Clock B strikes every [B] hours, and Clock C strikes every [C] hours. All three strike together at 12:00 noon. When will they next all strike together?
templates.explanation: Next time all strike together = LCM([A],[B],[C]) hours after 12:00 noon.

templates.pattern: The angle between the hands of a clock is [A]° at [H]:[M]. Find all possible times in the same hour if the angle is the same.
templates.explanation: |30H - 5.5M| = [A]. Solve: 30H - 5.5M = [A] and 30H - 5.5M = -[A]. Two solutions per hour if both fall within the hour. M = (30H ∓ [A]) / 5.5.

templates.pattern: Today is [DAY]. What was the day [N] days before [M] days after [P] days before today?
templates.explanation: Net days = -[P] + [M] - [N] = [M]-[N]-[P] from today. Result mod 7 gives net offset.

templates.pattern: A clock is correct at [H]:00 AM. It loses [L] seconds every [N] minutes. At what time will it next show the exact correct time? (12-hour clock)
templates.explanation: Clock loses [L]/[N] seconds per minute = [L]/([N]×60) minutes per minute. To fall back 12 hours (720 min), takes 720/([L]/([N]×60)) = 720×[N]×60/[L] real minutes.

templates.pattern: In a [Y]-year span starting from [Y1] (a leap year), how many times does Feb 29 occur?
templates.explanation: In 100 years: 24 leap years (not 25 because century year 2100 not leap). In 200 years: 48. In 400 years: 97. In 10 years (2000-2009): 3 (2000,2004,2008). In 50 years: 12. In 28 years: 7.

templates.pattern: A digital clock uses segments to display time HH:MM. At [H]:[M], how many total segments are lit if each digit uses 7-segment display?
What is the day on [D] [MONTH] [Y]? Use the formula: Day = (d + m + y + y/4 - 2×C + C/4) mod 7, where January and February are treated as months 11 and 12 of previous year.
templates.explanation: Apply Zeller's congruence or Doomsday algorithm for the given date.

templates.pattern: The time on a clock is [H]:[M]. What time did the clock show [T] minutes ago, and what will it show [T] minutes later?
templates.explanation: [T] min ago: subtract [T] from [H]:[M], borrow hours as needed. [T] min later: add [T] to [H]:[M], carry hours as needed.

templates.pattern: If Jan 1 of year [Y] is [DAY], and the year is a leap year, what day is Dec 31 of year [Y]?
templates.explanation: Leap year = 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 days. Dec 31 = Jan 1 + 365 days into the year = Jan 1 + (366-1) days = Jan 1 + 365 mod 7 = Jan 1 + 1 day. Wait — Dec 31 is day 366. From Jan 1 (day 1) to Dec 31 (day 366) = 365 days later. 365 mod 7 = 1. So Dec 31 = [DAY] + 1.

templates.pattern: A clock is placed facing a mirror. The mirror image shows [H]:[M]. If the time is between [T1] and [T2], what is the actual time?
templates.explanation: Mirror time formula: Actual = 11:60 - mirror reading (if result ≥ 12, subtract 12). 11:60 - [H]:[M].

templates.pattern: Ravi says: 'The day before yesterday was [DAY1].' Suresh heard this [N] days later. According to Suresh, what day was the day before yesterday when Ravi spoke, from Suresh's current perspective?
templates.explanation: Ravi spoke on [DAY1]+2. Suresh is now [N] days after Ravi spoke. Suresh's 'day before yesterday' = Suresh's today - 2 = ([DAY1]+2+[N]) - 2 = [DAY1]+[N].
